github.scope: Read-only live GitHub peer research for an English-first refinement of daxuan-science-assets. No peer code executed; no prose or assets copied.

current_package_observations.display_name: The current README and SKILL title are Chinese; the invocation slug daxuan-science-assets is already English.
current_package_observations.first_run: README clearly separates native SVG authoring, brief initialization and optional raster-reference generation. Installation is local-source based.
current_package_observations.assets: Three native-vector fixtures are documented as fixtures rather than image-model outputs.
current_package_observations.refinement_target: Translate the public-facing package and examples to English while preserving the scientific-asset scope and stable invocation slug.

channels: GitHub REST API via gh api
method.failure_handling: Three initial raw.githubusercontent.com requests timed out at 20 seconds; switched to GitHub API successfully. Did not execute peer tools or installation commands.

peers.name: ScanSci SVG
peers.positioning: Scientific SVG creation, semantic editing, reuse, conversion and composition from text, images and existing figures.
observations: The English brand plus format suffix makes the name recognisable even though most prose is Chinese.
The README places a real natural-language invocation before manual installation details.
Named object parts and subsequent edits are explained in terms of what the user wants to change.
Before/after cases link directly to downloadable SVG and record sources, licences and visible simplification limits.
Existing vector source is preferred before bitmap reconstruction; scientific, visual and editing checks are separated.
adopt: Retain a stable English slug and add a clear English display name.
Put one immediately usable invocation and one downloadable example on the first screen.
Explain semantic groups as practical editing actions.
do_not_copy: Much broader figure, PPTX, animation and publishing scope.
Unlicensed prose/assets; no repository-wide licence is declared.
peers.limits: Source review only; no output benchmarking or editor-import test performed.

peers.name: schematic-figure
peers.positioning: Code-native scientific schematic figures as SVG, PDF and PNG, with planning, rendering and checks.
observations: The hyphenated functional English name maps directly to the job.
README opens with the editable deliverable, then a comparison slideshow with attribution and a scope limitation.
Usage examples state scientific description, style, size and effort level.
The SKILL distinguishes design, replicate, describe and revise modes, with a brief and source-backed facts before drawing.
It reports which components of its own benchmark did and did not change the judge score.
adopt: Lead with editable output rather than a generic quality claim.
Keep a concise route table and a small complete example.
Pair claimed benefits with their actual evidence limits.
do_not_copy: Full-figure multi-draft workflow for every independent asset.
Browser/Node/Blender engine dependencies when the small SVG route is sufficient.
Peer benchmark claims as our own performance evidence.
peers.limits: Benchmark figures and scores are peer-reported; not independently reproduced.

peers.name: scientific-schematics
peers.positioning: Hosted image generation of scientific diagram PNG drafts with a bounded review/refinement loop.
observations: Current source explicitly says the output is raster PNG with no vector path or DPI control.
Quick Start distinguishes illustrative paid generation commands from offline request-contract tests.
When review cannot run, the image is retained with null score and an explicit unchecked status.
README provides cross-runtime discovery and a catalog rather than requiring all scientific dependencies.
adopt: Keep reference-image generation optional and distinguish it from final vector authorship.
Label unavailable model checks and preserve generated work without invented review scores.
do_not_copy: Raster PNG as the final product for an editable SVG request.
Numeric model-review thresholds as scientific validity or publisher acceptance.
Library-wide scale or adoption signals as evidence about this single skill.
peers.limits: Repository stars belong to the entire multi-skill library. Paid provider calls not reproduced.

peers.name: transparent-icons
peers.positioning: Scientific PNG icons with native alpha using a shared image backend and project theme.
observations: Its name immediately names the product and the desired background behaviour.
Theme, model and backend settings live outside the natural-language prompt.
Native alpha is preserved; removal fallback is described explicitly rather than always thresholding away light detail.
Includes a template list, a one-icon smoke route, a small icon-set example and explicit backend selection.
adopt: Separate colour roles from geometry and reference prompts.
Show a one-asset run before batch examples.
State actual alpha verification distinctly from a request for transparency.
do_not_copy: A mandatory sister-skill theme dependency for this self-contained local package.
New external backends in a naming/localisation refinement.
peers.limits: Backend and alpha behaviour are read from current source, not provider-tested in this review.

peers.name: svg-figure
peers.positioning: Hand-authored SVG conventions and explicit editor handoff, with new Python-generated figures routed to svg-primitives.
observations: The source starts by explaining when this skill is appropriate and when to use another route.
A canonical executable example is linked alongside the maintained expected SVG.
Editor handoff requirements are separate from the design master and validator guarantees.
Runtime-specific syntax is moved to host adapters in the wider figures plugin.
adopt: Make native-vector scope clear before listing capabilities.
Keep examples reproducible and paired with expected outputs.
Do not claim Illustrator/Affinity import success from structural validation alone.
do_not_copy: Embedding raster icon images in the SVG final asset.
Broader arrows/labels/layout engine for a single isolated object.
Cross-runtime support claims without actual installation checks.
peers.limits: Editor behaviour claims are peer-authored; no editor import was performed.

recommended_naming.tagline: Editable scientific SVG assets for research flowcharts.
recommended_naming.rationale: The display name is fully English, retains the owner brand, and matches the already-installed invocation slug. The tagline carries the transparent/native-vector constraints without making the name unwieldy.
avoid: A new slug only for cosmetic reasons, which would create migration friction.
Publication-quality or scientifically accurate as unqualified promises.
A name implying a complete figure-layout or mechanism-discovery suite.

bounded_refinement_recommendations: Translate SKILL.md, README, reference documents, interface metadata and active example labels to natural English as one language/identity refinement.
Keep code interfaces, SVG IDs, palette role names, invocation slug and asset geometry stable.
Put a short text-to-native-SVG invocation first, with brief-init and optional reference-model caveats visible below.
Make gallery labels English and retain the honest distinction between white presentation background and transparent single assets.
Keep one reproducible documented example and live command validation; do not add a suite, provider or publishing action in this pass.
github.evidence_caveat: These are source and packaging observations, not a controlled performance comparison. Repository stars are dated snapshots; installs were not measured and must not be inferred from stars.

catalogs.scope: Read-only ecosystem comparison for English naming, first-run clarity, and reproducible evidence. No peer code executed or skill installed.

peers.name: Transparent Icons
peers.type: direct task peer; different final format
peers.positioning: Flat scientific PNG icons with transparent backgrounds and a project palette.

metrics.meaning: Catalog installs displayed by skills CLI on check date, not a quality score.

peers.why_clear: The English name states both the deliverable and transparency. The first paragraph names scientific objects and figure use. A single-subject command and a three-icon example expose the actual artifact paths.
keep_or_adapt: Use a compact English title followed by a literal promise: transparent, editable SVG assets for research workflows.
Keep palette/theme independent of individual prompts.
Keep a real reproducible example script and distinguish a smoke run from a paid generation run.
Actually check alpha rather than infer transparency from a prompt.
reject: PNG as final deliverable because the user needs native editable SVG.
Automatic near-white threshold removal as proof of editable geometry.
Its sibling-plugin and shared-library dependencies for this deliberately standalone asset skill.
peers.limits: Source inspected; backend generation not run. Claims about model quality, alpha generation, or timing remain upstream claims.

peers.name: SVG Figure
peers.positioning: Hand-authoring SVG conventions and editor handoff for complete schematics.

metrics.meaning: Catalog installs displayed by skills CLI on check date, not a quality score.

peers.why_clear: English title plus explicit use/route-away lists quickly separate hand authored SVG, code-driven SVG, plots, and pictorial icons. File-level examples and the editor-prep command expose a visible handoff artifact.
keep_or_adapt: Named top-level groups per semantic part.
Concrete exported colors and editor-safe geometry.
Separate editable master from derived preview.
State editor-import checks only if actually run.
reject: Its suggestion to place raster icons through <image> as the final asset route.
Full figure composition, labels, arrows, journal font checks and orchestration dependencies for a single-object asset tool.
peers.limits: Source inspected; no Illustrator/Affinity import was performed in this research task.

peers.name: Scientific Graphical Abstract Skill
peers.positioning: AI-assisted editable SVG graphical abstracts, charts, and diagrams.

metrics.meaning: Different public catalog counters returned by detail endpoint; do not combine or treat as test scores.

peers.why_clear: Plain English task name, scenario-oriented usage, and an explicit SVG output contract. A reader can see what kind of output is intended without understanding the implementation.
keep_or_adapt: A short user prompt immediately after installation.
Input-to-file examples that explicitly name the editable SVG artifact.
reject: Broad all-chart/all-model/publication-ready claims without locally demonstrated evidence.
Full graphical abstracts and data charts, which would widen this user-requested asset-only scope.
peers.limits: Catalog description and metadata inspected, not the installed implementation. No measured output, provider trial, or reproducibility claim.

peers.name: Algorithmic Art
peers.positioning: Seeded generative art with interactive parameter exploration.
peers.why_clear: A literal English task name and an explicit output list (.md, .html, .js). The artifact workflow makes the result reproducible with seeds and adjustable parameters.
keep_or_adapt: List actual output files rather than vague capability bullets.
Keep tunable parameters separate from geometry and preserve reproducibility.
reject: Long artistic philosophy requirements and seeded randomness for scientific anatomical accuracy.
Runtime-specific branding for the core portable instructions.
peers.limits: Source inspected; no art generated. This is a presentation/workflow pattern reference, not a scientific illustration quality baseline.

peers.name: agent-browser
peers.positioning: Browser automation CLI for AI agents.
peers.why_clear: The README opens with a literal one-line purpose, visible license/version/skill-directory badges, installation, and a quick start that ends in a real screenshot artifact. It distinguishes requirements by install route. Its discovery stub routes to documentation matching the installed CLI version.
keep_or_adapt: One literal English sentence explaining the user outcome.
One recommended install route and a small first-run command sequence producing an inspectable preview.
Separate runtime requirements from optional capabilities.
Keep validation instructions versioned with the package.
reject: Its tool-preference instruction and broad browser actions; unrelated to scientific asset authoring.
Unnecessary CLI size or browser runtime dependency.
peers.limits: README and skill source inspected; no browser tool installed or executed. No claim of a measured conversion/install advantage.

recommendation.name: Daxuan Science Assets
recommendation.reason: Fully English while preserving the existing slug, installation path, and user ownership; a rename need not break invocation.
recommendation.one_line: Transparent, editable SVG assets for scientific workflow diagrams.
recommendation.first_prompt: Use $daxuan-science-assets to create a warm-gold liver asset with a transparent background, editable parts, and no labels or arrows.
recommendation.single_facet: English product surface: title, metadata, workflow instructions, references, README, example labels, generated artifact text, and installation handoff. Preserve geometry, palette, CLI commands, final SVG contract and scope.
proof_to_add: Render the same three real fixtures and compare geometry/alpha with baseline.
Replay one new-asset prompt and one existing-SVG recolor prompt, explicitly labeling dry-run or provider execution.
Regenerate English showcase from a checked-in script and retain actual image files.
Do not claim provider-backed imagery, blind preference or editor import validation until performed.
